findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes non-SMS and already-scheduled reminders
findings.body: The second branch of the cleanup `deleteMany` has only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`. It is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or `scheduled: false`, so this SMS cron will delete any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, including non-SMS reminders if the field is used elsewhere, and including rows that are already marked as scheduled. Deleting a scheduled row drops its provider reference (for example the Twilio SID) while the provider-side message may still be queued, and it can no longer be cancelled through the normal workflow path. Add the method and unscheduled predicates to this branch.

findings.title: retryCount increment is a lost-update race under overlapping cron runs
findings.body: On failure, both paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read before the network call. The cron endpoint has no lock or claim preventing overlapping invocations. Two runs can process the same unscheduled reminder, both call Twilio (causing duplicate SMS), and both write the same incremented value. As a result, two failures can leave `retryCount` at 1 instead of 2, so the reminder is retried more often than intended and may never reach the deletion threshold. Use an atomic update such as `{ increment: 1 }` and claim the row (e.g. conditional update or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) before sending.

findings.title: Retry update failure can abort the whole reminder batch
findings.body: The new `retryCount` update inside the `catch` block is not itself protected. If it fails, for example because another cron invocation already deleted the row or because of a transient database error, the exception escapes the catch, aborts the `for` loop, and prevents every remaining due reminder from being processed. The endpoint then returns 500 instead of continuing with the rest of the batch. Perform this update in its own try/catch or use `updateMany` so one stale row cannot break processing of other reminders.

findings.title: Post-send database errors cause duplicate SMS sends
findings.body: The `try` block wraps both `twilio.scheduleSMS` and the subsequent database update. If Twilio successfully schedules the SMS but the database update fails, execution enters this catch, increments `retryCount`, and leaves `scheduled` false without persisting `scheduledSMS.sid`. On the next cron run the same reminder is still considered unscheduled and the SMS is sent again, producing a duplicate message to the recipient. Persist the provider SID independently of the update failure, or mark the reminder as scheduled once Twilio confirms the send.
